title: Should You Get a COVID Shot This Fall? The 2026–27 Vaccines Are Here
excerpt: Four updated vaccines targeting the XFG variant won FDA approval for the 2026–27 season, with eligibility centered on older adults and people with underlying conditions.
body:
• The FDA has approved four updated COVID-19 vaccines for the 2026–2027 season, all targeting the JN.1-lineage XFG variant, and shots are expected to reach pharmacies and clinics within days.
  • Eligibility focuses on adults 65 and older and younger people with underlying conditions that raise the risk of severe COVID-19, with age cutoffs varying by vaccine.
  • The lineup covers Moderna's Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE, Pfizer-BioNTech's Comirnaty, and Novavax's protein-based Nuvaxovid.
  • State rules and insurer coverage will shape who can actually get a shot — and when — so checking with your clinic or pharmacy now is the practical first step.

Fall is coming, and with it a fresh round of COVID-19 vaccines. The Food and Drug Administration has approved four updated shots for the 2026–2027 season — two from Moderna, one from Pfizer-BioNTech, and one from Novavax-Sanofi — and the agency says doses should begin reaching pharmacies and health care providers across the United States within days. Here is what matters for your household this season.

What changed in this year's formula

All four vaccines are monovalent shots targeting the JN.1-lineage XFG variant, the lineage currently most prevalent globally. The FDA's vaccine advisory committee made the strain recommendation in late May 2026, and the agency then communicated the formula to manufacturers as the basis for the season. As with every annual update, the formula is a best target for the coming months rather than a guarantee of a perfect match — the virus keeps evolving between design and delivery — but it is intended to track the strains people are most likely to encounter this fall and winter.

The practical takeaway: protection from earlier doses wanes after about four to six months, according to public health guidance, so an updated shot is the mechanism for entering the respiratory-virus season current rather than relying on last year's immunity.

Who is eligible — and for which shot

Eligibility continues to focus on adults 65 and older and younger people with underlying medical conditions that put them at higher risk of severe COVID-19, though the exact age floors vary by product:

  • Comirnaty (Pfizer-BioNTech): adults 65 and older, and people ages 5 and older with at least one underlying condition.
  • Spikevax (Moderna): adults 65 and older, and people ages 6 months and older with at least one underlying condition.
  • mNEXSPIKE (Moderna): adults 65 and older, and people ages 12 through 64 with at least one underlying condition.
  • Nuvaxovid (Novavax): adults 65 and older, and people ages 12 and older with at least one underlying condition.

Comirnaty, Spikevax and mNEXSPIKE are mRNA vaccines; Nuvaxovid is protein-based, which matters for the small group of people who prefer or need a non-mRNA option.

"A strain/formula update helps guide the vaccine design for the coming season, but it does not replace the risk-based approach to deciding who should get an updated shot and when."

— FDA guidance framing, per the 2026–2027 formula recommendation

Timing, availability and the fine print

Clinics and purchasing groups began taking pre-bookings in June, and insurers have broadly indicated they will cover the season's vaccines — but the on-the-ground rollout will vary by clinic, region and state rules. Some states' regulations may limit whether children and younger adults without underlying conditions can receive a shot, so the most useful step is a quick call or portal check with your pharmacy or primary care provider rather than assuming eligibility.

Availability may also be staggered, with some sites prioritizing high-risk groups first. If you fall into a priority group — over 65, immunocompromised, or managing a chronic condition — booking early in the season puts you ahead of the late-fall surge when respiratory viruses typically gather steam.

What to watch for your family

COVID remains a meaningful risk for severe illness in older adults and the immunocompromised, and this year's narrower eligibility framing puts the decision squarely on risk assessment rather than a universal campaign. For households with grandparents, expect the question to come up at holiday planning: the updated shot is the current-season answer, and getting it weeks before Thanksgiving and Diwali gatherings gives protection time to build.

And if you are traveling internationally this fall — including the busy India routes, where long flights put you in close quarters with hundreds of fellow passengers — an updated dose is one of the few levers you control. The vaccines do not promise perfect protection against infection, but the consistent record across seasons is that they lower the odds of severe disease, which is the outcome that matters.
